name: fetchLater
plain: Queues a request now that the browser sends later, even if the page closes first.
meaning: Gives analytics a reliable way to report at page end. The browser sends it after a chosen delay or when the page is discarded or goes into bfcache. Chrome shipped it in version 135 (Apr 2025).

access.persistence: Sent by the browser at the delay or page end; can be cancelled by the page
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can queue a report now and have the browser send it later, even after you close
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you use a page that sets up a delayed report
can: Queue a request that the browser sends when the page closes
Send it at a time the page sets
Update or cancel the queued report while the page is open
cannot: Send the report forever; the browser sends it after a limit
Work in Firefox, Safari or iPhone browsers
Show a prompt or any sign that a report is waiting
limits.differs: Only Chrome, Edge and Chrome on Android support it.

story.what_it_is: Lets a page queue a message that the browser sends later, even if you close the page first.

marketing.name: fetchLater API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes it as a way to queue a request that goes out later, so end of visit reports are not lost.

story.for_you: You never see it. A page can write a note now, and the browser sends it after a delay or when you leave. If you close the tab, it still goes out.
story.for_makers: End of visit data is the hardest to send, since pages die without warning. fetchLater gives analytics a reliable last send, and the browser picks a safe time. It beats old tricks that slowed down pages.

use_cases.example: A web speed tool queues a report of your page load and layout shifts and sends it when you leave.
An ad network queues a report about how long an ad was visible and sends it as the tab closes.
A browser game queues your session stats, such as time played and level reached, and sends them after you quit.
A video site queues the total watch time and buffering counts, sent when you leave.
A store queues the final cart state so a cart reminder can be sent even if you abandon the tab.
An app queues error logs from a session and sends them with the closing report to Sentry or a custom server.

risks: Data goes out after you leave
Only in some browsers so far

technical_bounds: Cookies for the target origin are sent

history.change: Shipped as the successor to unload beacons
